Speaker 2 (Chairman & Managing Director) Textile tailwinds are often seasonal, festival demand, market cycles.
Margins & costs: Also, EBITDA at 50%, in a normal textile company, depreciation cost and interest cost are high, and taxation comes in, so PAT is lower.
If I am operating at 50% EBITDA margin, my PAT would typically be ~15%, but because I don't have these three costs, EBITDA largely flows through, so PAT margin can be ~35% to 40%.
Once we scale, EBITDA margin might shrink by about 5-7%, but overall EBITDA-to-PAT journey remains strong because of the advantages we have in interest, depreciation, and taxation.
Capex & expansion: They had a capacity of 35 million meters in denim fabrics, and almost 18 million meters in non- denim capacity.
That's why, with our 35 million meter denim capacity, the transformation to non-denim does not require heavy capex.
Speaker 2 (Chairman & Managing Director) Denim-to-non-denim conversion won't require more than about ₹10 crore capex, and that capex will be funded by selling machines that are not required.
Balance sheet & cash: To achieve about ₹100 crore annual revenue, working capital required is around ₹15-₹20 crore, which we initially infused.
Speaker 2 (Chairman & Managing Director) Originally, the old promoters had very high debt, more than about ₹300 crore, and that was settled by them.
So customer base is diversified. up to ₹100 crore revenue, we don't require significant working capital.
Risks & challenges: Also, the cash flow cycle becomes better because credits are very limited, credit risk is lower.
